chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): Is the testimony of the trustee for the deceased accepted regarding a debt he has upon a man, along with another just witness? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: If another just witness testifies with him, then it is upon the claimant to swear an oath.

And he wrote: Is it permissible for the trustee to testify for the heir of the deceased, whether young or old, regarding a right he has upon the deceased or upon someone else, and he is the holder for the young heir, and not a holder for the adult? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Yes, it is befitting for the trustee to testify with the truth and not conceal the testimony.
And he wrote: Or is the testimony of the trustee accepted against the deceased, along with another just witness? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Yes, after an oath.

key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: Trustee or executor of the deceased's estate

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting a trustee's testimony for a deceased person's debts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the evidentiary weight of a trustee (al-wasi) in debt claims, requiring an additional just witness and the claimant's oath to validate the testimony. It further establishes the trustee's duty to testify truthfully for both minor and adult heirs, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the trustee's dual role as both custodian and witness in posthumous financial settlements.

en.hubeali: ‘Muhammad Bin Al-Hassan wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Would the testimony of the trustee for the deceased be accepted with the debts for him upon a man with another just witness. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘When another just witness is with him, so it is upon the claimant to swear an oath’.

And he wrote, ‘Is it allowed for the trustee that he should testify for the inheritors of the deceased, young or old, with a right of his upon the deceased, or upon someone else, and he is the holder for the young inheritors, and he is not a holder for the elder ones?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Yes. It is befitting for the trustee that he should testify with the truth, and he should not conceal the testimony’.
And he wrote, ‘Or is the testimony of the trustee acceptable against the deceased, with another just witness?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Yes, from after an oath’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has said that

Muhammad ibn al-Hassan once wrote to abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asking if testimony of executor of the will is acceptable for the deceased about a loan that a man owes to the deceased with one more just witness. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, signed the answer that said: ‘If one more just man testifies with him then the plaintiff must take an oath.’

He also wrote asking if it is permissible for an executor of the will to testify for an heir of the deceased, small or an adult in a right for him on the deceased or on others and he is the one who takes possession for the heir who is a minor and not an adult. He (the Imam), signed the answer that said, ‘Yes, it is proper for an executor of the will to testify for a right and he must not hide a testimony.’

He wrote asking that if the testimony of an executor of the will along with the testimony of another just man is admissible against the deceased. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, signed the answer that said, ‘Yes, it is acceptable with an oath.’”
